title: Cardiomyopathy diagnosis model from endomyocardial biopsy specimens: Appropriate feature space and class boundary in small sample size data
study_context: Texture-feature classification of 60 myocardial microscopic images from six autopsy subjects: two HCM/disarray, two borderline and two noncardiac-death controls.
population_or_data: Texture-feature classification of 60 myocardial microscopic images from six autopsy subjects: two HCM/disarray, two borderline and two noncardiac-death controls.
task: Texture-feature classification of 60 myocardial microscopic images from six autopsy subjects: two HCM/disarray, two borderline and two noncardiac-death controls.
method: Texture features, feature selection/dimensional compression, and classical classifiers including linear SVM.
main_findings: Despite biopsy-oriented framing, the reported experiment used 60 microscopic images from six autopsy subjects; it did not test transfer to living-patient endomyocardial biopsies.
limitations: Selected-page review, not full-paper audit. PDF pages 1, 16, 26 and extracted text visually checked on 2026-10-07.

Six patients and microscopic fields are not an independent clinical biopsy cohort. No biopsy/autopsy joint-learning benefit, rejection discrimination, WSI generalization, or fully audited patient-separated validation is established. High reported image-level performance must not be transferred to SMC.
does_not_establish: Six patients and microscopic fields are not an independent clinical biopsy cohort. No biopsy/autopsy joint-learning benefit, rejection discrimination, WSI generalization, or fully audited patient-separated validation is established. High reported image-level performance must not be transferred to SMC.
relevance_to_project: A small-model cardiac autopsy example whose actual specimen origin and number of independent patients must remain explicit.
